candidates.label: Khirbet Karraza (Korazim)
candidates.support: Wikidata's coordinate agrees with the Digital Atlas of the Roman Empire's point to within about 30 meters.

summary.text: Chorazin was a Galilean town near Capernaum that, according to Matthew and Luke, Jesus rebuked for failing to repent despite witnessing his miracles there.

history.text: The site, now a national park, preserves the remains of a Jewish town including a basalt-stone synagogue generally dated to the third or fourth century AD, built on a settlement with earlier Roman-period occupation layers beneath it.

scripture.textWEB: “Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago in sackcloth and ashes.
“Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the mighty works had been done in Tyre and Sidon which were done in you, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
